quote: The wounded and dead were seen strewn amongst the grass and grain
says: On 3 July, as the Confederate column fell back, the wounded and dead lay among standing grass and grain on the plain between the lines (Jacobs, who watched from the town).
feature: grass and grain between Seminary Ridge and Cemetery Ridge on 3 July
note: Not stated: which grain, nor which fields. Jacobs, a professor of mathematics at Pennsylvania College, who watched the fighting from the town and wrote his account within months (1864).

quote: The scarred timber in the vicinity well attests the obstinacy and effectiveness with which our men fought.
says: The timber on and about Culp's Hill, where Greene's brigade fought on the evening of 2 July, was scarred by the fire.
feature: Culp's Hill timber after the fighting of 2 July

when.basis: the fight of the evening of 2 July; the book is of 1864

note: The share of trees scarred is not stated. Jacobs, a professor of mathematics at Pennsylvania College, who watched the fighting from the town and wrote his account within months (1864).

quote: our batteries, placed in a grove near Bryan's house, opened upon them
says: On 3 July the Union batteries that fired on the advancing column stood in a grove near the Brien house (Jacobs's spelling is Bryan).
feature: the grove near the Brien house
note: Placed on the nearest wood to the farmstead within 260 m (no direction is given). Jacobs, a professor of mathematics at Pennsylvania College, who watched the fighting from the town and wrote his account within months (1864).

quote: was seen to emerge from the wooded crest of the Seminary ridge, just to the south of McMillan's orchard
says: On 3 July Pickett's division came out of the wooded crest of Seminary Ridge just south of McMillan's orchard: the orchard stood and the crest was wooded.
feature: McMillan's orchard and the wooded crest of Seminary Ridge
note: Placed on the nearest orchard to the McMillan farmstead within 450 m. Jacobs, a professor of mathematics at Pennsylvania College, who watched the fighting from the town and wrote his account within months (1864).

quote: drove the Rebels down the rocky front of that hill, across the valley below, and over the next hill into the woods beyond
says: At 6 p.m. on 2 July Crawford's division drove the Confederates down the rocky front of Little Round Top, across the valley below it, and over the next hill into the woods beyond.
feature: the rocky front of Little Round Top
note: "That hill" is the Little Round Top of the sentence before. Rocky says nothing of trees on it. Jacobs, a professor of mathematics at Pennsylvania College, who watched the fighting from the town and wrote his account within months (1864).
